field.label: Enabled
field.help: Block what the lists below name. Off, the rules are gone at the next filter reload and nothing is cut; the lists stay chosen.

field.label: Address lists
field.help: Public lists of addresses to block, each fetched by the firewall into an alias of its own (blocklists_...), as often as Fetch the lists says. ThreatFox: command-and-control addresses is fetched only with an abuse.ch Auth-Key, the next setting. The Lists tab says what each one is and whose terms it comes under.

field.label: abuse.ch Auth-Key
field.help: For the list ThreatFox: command-and-control addresses, in Address lists: abuse.ch serves it only with the Auth-Key of an abuse.ch account, free at auth.abuse.ch (in its profile, under Optional). The firewall sends the key to abuse.ch in the address of each download, over HTTPS with the server's certificate checked, as abuse.ch asks, and nothing else of its own - no address of its networks, no log, no setting; abuse.ch sees the request come from its public address, as any server does. The key is kept in the configuration and never shown on this page again: the field says whether one is saved; leave it empty to keep the key, or take it out with Remove the key. ThreatFox's whole export is fetched once a day, as abuse.ch asks, and its recent additions as often as Fetch the lists says. For commercial use abuse.ch may ask for a paid subscription.

field.label: Fetch the lists
field.help: How often the firewall fetches each address list again. Each list keeps a floor of its own: Spamhaus DROP once a day, as Spamhaus asks, and Emerging Threats and CINS Army, which publish no rule, once a day too. A list is fetched at once, whatever its floor, when its alias is made again: the list chosen again, or the plugin or the alias switched off and on. ThreatFox is fetched by the plugin itself, as abuse.ch asks: its whole export once a day, whatever this says, and its recent additions as often as this says, an hour apart at the least. A change reaches the lists at the next Apply, and at the plugin's update.

field.label: Countries
field.help: Block every address registered to these countries, in a GeoIP alias. It needs a GeoIP source set in Firewall: Aliases: GeoIP settings; without one the alias stays empty.

field.label: Direction
field.help: Inbound only: nothing from a listed address gets in. Both ways: nothing inside can reach one either.

field.label: Log blocked packets
field.help: Write every packet the rules block to the firewall log. A long list blocks a lot. With Both ways, a device trying to reach a command-and-control list (Feodo Tracker, ThreatFox) is logged whatever this says, by its own address, so it can be found - where it comes in on an inside interface: one with an address of its own, not taken by DHCP, PPPoE or the like, and no gateway on it. Elsewhere (a VPN group, or a LAN with a router behind it set as a gateway) it is blocked all the same, and logged only as this says.

field.label: Cut open connections
field.help: A block rule stops new connections only. With this on, a connection already open to or from an address a list has just gained is cut within a minute. On a Sophos XGS with os-xgs-npu's Cut in hardware on, and outbound blocked too, it is also dropped on the coprocessor at once, and kept dropped there while its sender goes on sending: an address that leaves a list does not hand it back (XGS: Offloaded Flows does).

field.label: TLS fingerprints (JA4)
field.help: Cut every TLS connection whose client shows one of these JA4 fingerprints, separated by commas - it names the program, whatever server it goes to. Read from the Intrusion Detection's TLS log, which must carry the ja4 field; the JA4 tab says what is missing and which fingerprints are seen.

field.label: Block what the IPS drops
field.help: Block for a while the source of what the Intrusion Detection's IPS policy drops: each alert it logs as blocked over a connection it saw established puts the address that sent the dropped traffic into a list of the plugin's own, IPS drops (blocklists_ids), blocked like the other lists in the Direction set here. Its open connections are cut where Cut open connections is on - on a Sophos XGS with os-xgs-npu's Cut in hardware on, and Direction Both ways, on the coprocessor too. Only in IPS mode (Netmap or Divert): IDS mode logs nothing as blocked. An alert's source can be forged, so only an alert over TCP, on a connection whose application protocol Suricata recognised (it does so only once the connection is established with the real address) and with packets both ways past the handshake, enters: a lone SYN, a scan's or one forged with another's address, never does; nor one of Suricata's own decoder, stream and application-layer event rules (signature ids 2200000-2299999), which drop one packet, not a connection. Never entered: an address of the firewall's own (every interface's, its virtual IPs and the external addresses of its 1:1 and outbound NAT), loopback, multicast, unspecified or link-local; its gateways and their monitor addresses; its DNS servers; its VPN peers (IPsec remote gateways, WireGuard endpoints, OpenVPN remotes); an address with a connection open to its web GUI or SSH; and what Never block holds. Taken from the moment it is turned on: nothing logged before. At most 200 addresses enter at a reading of the log, every three seconds, and 10,000 are held: past them, those dropped longest ago leave first. Turned off, every address leaves at once. Where /var is kept in memory, a reboot starts the list empty.

field.label: Keep an address (minutes)
field.help: How long an address stays in IPS drops after the last alert that put it there: 60 minutes by default, 5 to 10080 (a week). Each new drop of it starts the time again, and a change here applies to the addresses already held too.

field.label: Outside addresses only
field.help: Leave out every address inside the firewall's own networks, so a false alarm never cuts a device of yours off for the time above: every network connected to the firewall (each interface's address and prefix, IPv4 and IPv6, WAN's too), its delegated IPv6 prefixes, its VPN tunnel and remote networks, its static routes' networks, and the private ones - 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, the shared 100.64/10 (where VPN overlays live too) and IPv6's unique local fc00::/7. An address held that is now inside them leaves. Off, a device inside is blocked as well when the IPS drops what it sends.

field.label: Never block
field.help: Addresses and networks never put into IPS drops, whatever the IPS drops from them - your own exceptions, such as a partner's or a monitoring service's: each entered on its own, as 198.51.100.7, 198.51.100.0/24 or 2001:db8::/48. An address held that is in them leaves at the next reading.
